title: Little Office of the Sick According to the Mozarabic Rite

introductoryNotes.text: From Breviarium Gothicum secundum regulam Beatissimi Isidori Archiepiscopi Hispalensis (1775).

Incipit Officium unius infirmi sive plurimorum infirmorum. Et dicitur officium istud in sexta feria. Quando non habuerit aliqua festa recitare, vel in alio tempore quando sibi placuerit recitare illud.
introductoryNotes.english: Here begins the office for one sick person or for several sick persons. This office is said on Friday, when there is no feast to recite, or at another time when one wishes to recite it.

blocks.source: Precámur, Domine, ut nos in ira tua non arguas: et furorem tuum in nos desaeviré non sinas: sed placidus corrector tolle peccandi usum; ne nos arguendo durius, propellas ad nihilum: Miserere ergo infirmitati nostrae: et famulorum tuorum, omnium fidelium infirmorum tuam imperti medelam: et quos cernis proprio turbari peccato, quietos deputa, misericorditer indulgendo.
blocks.english: We pray, O Lord, that Thou rebuke us not in Thine anger, and permit not Thy fury to rage against us: but as a gentle corrector take away the habit of sinning; lest by rebuking us too harshly Thou drive us to nothing. Have mercy therefore upon our weakness, and impart Thy remedy to Thy servants, all the sick faithful: and those whom Thou seest troubled by their own sin, reckon as at peace by mercifully forgiving them.

blocks.source: Omnipotens Dominus, qui fidelissimos famulos suos omnes fideles infirmos corporali corripit vulnere, ipse illos, et nos a corporis mentisque aegritudinibus expiet. ℟. Amen. Quique nostram in se suscepit infirmitatem, ipse nobis, et illis tribuat tolerantiae sine fine mercedem. ℟. Amen. Sic omnes in communi ejus pietas foveat; ut nec corrupta nostra salus desaeviat, nec desperationi infirmitas illata succumbat. ℟. Amen. Per misericordiam tuam Deus noster, qui es benedictus et omnia regis, in saecula saeculorum.
blocks.english: May the almighty Lord, who chastens His most faithful servants, all the sick faithful, with bodily wounds, Himself cleanse them and us from sickness of body and mind. ℟. Amen. And He who took our weakness upon Himself, may He grant us and them the everlasting reward of endurance. ℟. Amen. May His loving kindness cherish all alike, so that neither our impaired health may rage, nor inflicted sickness succumb to despair. ℟. Amen. Through Thy mercy, our God, who art blessed and rulest all things, forever and ever.

blocks.source: Miserere mei Deus secundum magnam misericordiam tuam et secundum multitudinem miserationum tuarum dele iniquitates meas. Usquequaque lava me ab iniustitia mea et a peccato meo munda me. Quoniam iniquitatem meam ego agnosco et peccatum meum contra me est semper. Tibi soli peccavi et malum coram te feci ut iustificeris in sermonibus tuis et vincas dum iudicaris. Ecce enim in iniquitatibus conceptus sum et in peccatis peperit me mater mea. Ecce enim veritatem dilexisti incerta et occulta sapientiae tuae manifestasti mihi. Asperges me hysopo et mundabor lavabis me et super nivem dealbabor. Auditui meo dabis gaudium et laetitiam et exultabunt ossa humiliata. Averte faciem tuam a peccatis meis et omnes iniquitates meas dele. Cor mundum crea in me Deus spiritum rectum innova in visceribus meis. Ne proicias me a facie tua spiritum sanctum tuum ne auferas a me. Redde mihi laetitiam salutaris tui spiritu principali confirma me. Doceam iniquos vias tuas et impii ad te convertentur. Libera me de sanguinibus Deus Deus salutis meae laudabit lingua mea iustitias tuas. Domine labia mea aperies et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam. Quoniam si voluisses sacrificium dedissem utique holocaustis non delectaberis. Sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus cor contritum et humiliatum Deus non spernit. Benigne fac Domine in bona voluntate tua Sion ut aedificentur muri Hierusalem. Tunc acceptabis sacrificium iustitiae oblationes et holocausta tunc impones super altare tuum vitulos. Gloria et honor.
blocks.english: Have mercy upon me, O God, according to Thy great mercy, and according to the multitude of Thy mercies blot out my iniquities. Wash me utterly from my injustice, and cleanse me from my sin. For I acknowledge my iniquity, and my sin is always before me. Against Thee alone have I sinned and done evil before Thee, that Thou mayest be justified in Thy words and prevail when judged. For behold, I was conceived in iniquities, and in sins my mother bore me. For behold, Thou hast loved truth: Thou hast made known to me the uncertain and hidden things of Thy wisdom. Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed: Thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow. Thou shalt give joy and gladness to my hearing, and humbled bones shall exult. Turn Thy face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities. Create a clean heart in me, O God; renew a right spirit within me. Cast me not away from Thy face; take not Thy Holy Ghost from me. Restore to me the joy of Thy salvation; strengthen me with a sovereign spirit. Let me teach the wicked Thy ways, and the ungodly shall turn unto Thee. Deliver me from bloodshed, O God, God of my salvation; my tongue shall praise Thy justices. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips, and my mouth shall announce Thy praise. For hadst Thou desired sacrifice, I would indeed have given it: Thou wilt not delight in burnt offerings. A sacrifice to God is a troubled spirit: God despises not a contrite and humbled heart. Deal kindly, O Lord, in Thy good will with Sion, that the walls of Jerusalem may be built. Then shalt Thou accept the sacrifice of justice, offerings and burnt offerings: then shalt Thou lay calves upon Thine altar. Glory and honour.

blocks.source: Laudate Dominum de caelis laudate eum in excelsis. Laudate eum omnes angeli ejus laudate eum omnes virtutes ejus. Laudate eum sol et luna laudate eum omnes stellae et lumen. Laudate eum caeli caelorum et aquae quae super caelos sunt, laudent nomen Domini. Quia ipse dixit et facta sunt ipse mandavit et creata sunt. Statuit ea in aeternum et in saeculum saeculi praeceptum posuit et non praeteribit. Laudate Dominum a terra dracones et omnes abyssi. Ignis grando nix glacies spiritus tempestatis qui facitis verbum ejus. Montes et omnes colles ligna fructifera et omnes cedri. Bestiae et universa pecora serpentes et volucres pinnatae. Reges terrae et omnes populi principes et judices terrae. Juvenes et virgines seniores cum junioribus laudent nomen Domini. Quia exaltatum est nomen ejus solius confessio ejus super caelum et terram. Et exaltavit cornu populi sui hymnus omnibus sanctis ejus filiis populo appropinquanti sibi.
blocks.english: Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise Him in the heights. Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His powers. Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all ye stars and light. Praise Him, heavens of heavens; and let all waters above the heavens praise the name of the Lord: for He spoke and they were made; He commanded and they were created. He established them forever and ever: He gave a commandment, and it shall not pass away. Praise the Lord from the earth, dragons and all depths; fire, hail, snow, ice, storm winds that fulfil His word; mountains and all hills, fruitful trees and all cedars; beasts and all cattle, creeping things and winged birds. Kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and judges of the earth; young men and maidens, the old with the young, let them praise the name of the Lord: for His name alone is exalted, His praise above heaven and earth: and He has exalted the horn of His people. A hymn for all His saints, for the children, the people drawing near to Him.

blocks.source: Cantate Domino canticum novum laus ejus in Ecclesiis sanctorum. Laetetur Israel in eo qui fecit ipsum et filii Syon exultent super regem suum. Exultabunt sancti in gloria et laetabuntur in cubilibus suis. Exultationes Dei in faucibus eorum et gladii bis acuti in manibus eorum. Ad faciendam vindictam in nationibus increpationes in populis. Ad alligandos reges eorum in compedibus et nobiles eorum in vinculis ferreis. Ut fiat in eis judicium conscriptum gloria haec est omnibus sanctis ejus.
blocks.english: Sing unto the Lord a new song: His praise in the churches of saints. Let Israel rejoice in Him who made him; and let the sons of Sion exult in their King. Let them praise His name in the dance; let them sing unto Him with timbrel and psaltery. For the Lord is well pleased with His people, and has exalted the meek in salvation. The saints shall exult in glory; they shall rejoice upon their beds. The praises of God are in their throats, and two-edged swords in their hands: to execute vengeance upon nations, and rebukes upon peoples; to bind their kings in fetters, and their nobles in iron chains; to execute upon them the written judgment: this glory belongs to all His saints.

Et invocabitis me, et timebitis: orabitis me, et ego exaudiam vos. Quaeretis me, et invenietis: cum quaesieritis me in toto corde vestro, inveniar a vobis, ait Dominus omnipotens. ℟. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. Thanks be to God. Thus says the Lord: Behold, I shall visit you and raise you up, and establish my good word over you, and bring you back to this place. And ye shall invoke me, and fear: ye shall pray to me, and I shall hear you. Ye shall seek me and find me: when ye seek me with your whole heart, I shall be found by you, says the Lord almighty. ℟. Amen.
